extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, patent practitioners, and draughtsmen preparing U.S. patent drawings
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and regulatory requirements (37 CFR 1.84 and 1.85) for preparing, formatting, and correcting drawings submitted to the U.S. Patent and Trademark Office for utility, plant, and design applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indicia placement
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants are strongly encouraged to provide identifying information (indicia) on drawings to allow the Office to match a drawing sheet to the proper application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If indicia are provided on the front of drawings they must be placed on the front of each sheet and centered within the top margin so electronic and paper copies will include the indicia. If indicia are placed on the back, the drawings will not be objected to, but copies will not include the indicia. In U.S. national stage PCT applications the top of the drawing sheet may show the international publication number and date (not objectionable under 37 CFR 1.84(c)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Graphic forms allowed as drawings
rubrics_metrics.description: Chemical or mathematical formulae, tables, and waveforms may be submitted as drawings and are subject to the same requirements as drawings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each chemical or mathematical formula must be labeled as a separate figure, using brackets when necessary. Each group of waveforms must be a single figure with a common vertical axis (time horizontally); each individual waveform discussed in the specification must be identified with a separate letter designation adjacent to the vertical axis. Note: flow diagrams, waveforms, graphs, etc., cannot be in the specification and must be drawings. Computer program listings of 300 or fewer lines and 72 or fewer characters per line may be submitted as drawings (see 37 CFR 1.96). Nucleotide/amino acid sequence data may be submitted as drawings but sequence listing rules (37 CFR 1.821–1.825) still apply if thresholds are met.

rubrics_metrics.name: Paper type and condition
rubrics_metrics.description: Drawings must be on flexible, strong, white, smooth, non-shiny, durable paper; sheets must be reasonably free from cracks, creases, folds, erasures, alterations, overwritings, and interlineations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only one side of the sheet may be used. Photographs must meet sheet-size and margin requirements and paragraph (b) requirements for photographs. Special correction products (e.g., masking fluid) may be used if indelible and compliant. Partial waiver: while line drawings must be non-shiny, the Office will not object to photographs on glossy paper. Mounted photographs are precluded (Office will object to mounted photographs as of enforcement date); applicants are encouraged to transmit drawings by mail with protection or hand-carried rather than folding; faxing is allowed with payment of issue fee but may degrade quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Uniform sheet size
rubrics_metrics.description: All drawing sheets in an application must be the same size.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acceptable sizes: (1) 21.0 x 29.7 cm (A4) or (2) 21.6 x 27.9 cm (8½ x 11 inches). One of the shorter sides is regarded as the top. For PCT national-stage filings the International Bureau's A4 requirement means U.S. national stage drawings will be A4.

rubrics_metrics.name: Margins and scan target points
rubrics_metrics.description: Sheets must not contain frames around the sight but should have scan target points printed on two cater-corner margin corners; required minimum margins: top ≥ 2.5 cm, left ≥ 2.5 cm, right ≥ 1.5 cm, bottom ≥ 1.0 cm.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These margins leave a defined sight area (17.0 x 26.2 cm on A4, 17.6 x 24.4 cm on 8½ x 11). Scan target points facilitate scanning/printing and are desirable but not required ('should' indicates preference). Applicants may elect not to place scan target points; when adding or removing them for international vs U.S. filing, add/remove only to copies being filed with the Office as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Number and type of views required
rubrics_metrics.description: The drawing must contain as many views as necessary to show the invention; views may be plan, elevation, section, or perspective; detail views and enlarged views are allowed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All views must be grouped together, arranged without wasting space, preferably upright, clearly separated, and not included on sheets with specifications, claims, or abstract. Views must not be connected by projection lines or contain center lines. Waveforms may be connected by dashed lines to show relative timing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exploded views
rubrics_metrics.description: Exploded views showing separated parts to indicate relationship/order of assembly are permissible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When an exploded view appears on the same sheet as another figure it should be placed in brackets. Use brackets to embrace separated parts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Partial views and linking
rubrics_metrics.description: Partial views of large machines may be broken into partial views on a single sheet or extended over multiple sheets if understanding is not lost; partial views on separate sheets must be linkable edge-to-edge so no partial view contains parts of another partial view.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include a smaller-scale view showing the whole formed by partial views and indicating positions of parts shown. When a portion is enlarged for magnification, label the view and the enlarged view as separate views. Where views on two or more sheets form one complete view, arrange them so the complete figure can be assembled without concealing any part. Very long views may be divided vertically on a single sheet but relationships must be clear and unambiguous.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sectional (cross-sectional) views
rubrics_metrics.description: Section planes should be indicated on the view from which the section is cut by a broken line; ends of broken lines designated by numerals corresponding to the sectional view and with arrows indicating direction of sight; hatching must indicate sectioned portions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hatching must be regularly spaced oblique parallel lines spaced to be distinguishable; should not impede reference characters or lead lines; hatching may be broken off where reference characters are inserted; hatching preferably at 45° to principal lines. Cross-sections must show materials as in the view; different parts should be hatched consistently, juxtaposed different elements hatched at different angles. For large areas hatching may be confined to an edging. Different hatching types can denote material conventionally.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alternate position and moved-position depiction
rubrics_metrics.description: Moved positions may be shown by a broken line superimposed on a suitable view if not crowded; otherwise use a separate view.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure the moved position depiction does not crowd the drawing; use separate view when necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Modified forms
rubrics_metrics.description: Modified forms of construction must be shown in separate views.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinct embodiments should be clearly separated and labeled as separate views.

rubrics_metrics.name: Arrangement of views on sheet
rubrics_metrics.description: One view must not be placed upon or within the outline of another; all views on the same sheet should stand in the same direction and, if possible, so they can be read with the sheet upright.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If very wide views require rotating the sheet, the top may be on the right-hand side but words must appear horizontally left-to-right when either upright or turned so the top becomes the right side (except for standard scientific graphs). This allows rotation by 90° right while keeping text readable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Front page view suitability and selection
rubrics_metrics.description: One view should be suitable for inclusion on the front page of the patent application publication and patent as the illustration of the invention; applicant may suggest a single view by figure number.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant may indicate suggested front-page figure in the application transmittal letter, but the Office is not bound by the suggestion. The selected view should be at a scale that clearly illustrates details after up to two-thirds reduction (see 1.84(k)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Scale of drawings
rubrics_metrics.description: Drawings must be made to a scale large enough to show the mechanism without crowding when reduced to two-thirds in reproduction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indications such as 'actual size' or 'scale 1/2' are not permitted since they lose meaning with repro. Measurement indications like '←1 inch→' or '∠45°' are acceptable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Character of lines, numbers, and letters
rubrics_metrics.description: All drawings must be made by a process giving satisfactory reproduction characteristics: lines, numbers, and letters must be durable, clean, black (except color drawings), sufficiently dense and dark, uniformly thick and well-defined.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Line weight must permit adequate reproduction. Use continuous thick lines for edging/outlining and cross sections; continuous thin lines for leading lines, hatching outlines of adjoining elements; thin freehand lines for delimiting views/part sections; thin broken lines (short dashes) for hidden edges; dot-dash thin line for axes/planes of symmetry and extreme positions; thin line terminating in one heavy line for outlines of cross sections. Different line thicknesses may be used if they have different meanings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Shading
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of shading is encouraged if it aids understanding and does not reduce legibility; shading indicates surface/shape of spherical/cylindrical/conical elements; flat parts may be lightly shaded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Spaced thin lines for shading are preferred (as few as practicable) and must contrast with the rest of the drawing; light should come from the upper left at ~45°. Shading is preferred in perspective views but not for cross-sections (use hatching for cross-sections). Solid black shading not permitted except for bar graphs or color representation. Stippling and other techniques may be used when appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Symbols
rubrics_metrics.description: Graphical drawing symbols may be used for conventional elements when appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Elements illustrated by symbols must be adequately identified in the specification. Use universally recognized conventional symbols for known devices. Non-universal symbols may be used subject to Office approval if not likely to be confused and readily identifiable. See Appendix 3 for conventions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legends
rubrics_metrics.description: Suitable descriptive legends may be used subject to Office approval or may be required by the examiner; they should contain as few words as possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Words should not describe the figure itself (e.g., 'This is a bar graph' is disallowed). All text legends must be approved by the Office. Elements labeled in drawings must be adequately identified in the specification. Drawings cannot contain expressions contrary to morality/public order, trademarks/service marks unless applicant has proprietary interest, or any statement obviously irrelevant or unnecessary. Exception: the 'as few words as possible' guideline does not apply when the drawing is a computer screen image.

rubrics_metrics.name: Numbers, letters, and reference characters (general rules)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reference characters (numerals preferred), sheet numbers, and view numbers must be plain, legible, not used with brackets or enclosed outlines (e.g., encircled), and oriented in the same direction as the view; reference characters should follow the profile of the object.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: English alphabet must be used for letters except where customarily another alphabet (e.g., Greek) is used. Reference characters must be at least 0.32 cm (1/8 inch) high, should not interfere with comprehension, not cross or mingle with lines, and not be placed on hatched/shaded surfaces unless space left or hatching broken off. The same part shown in more than one view must have the same reference character; the same reference character must not designate different parts. Reference characters not mentioned in the description must not appear in the drawings; those mentioned in the description must appear in the drawings. Each element must be identified by a reference number except on design drawings. Avoid overuse of primed, subscript, or superscript characters as they can obfuscate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lead lines
rubrics_metrics.description: Lead lines are lines between reference characters and the referred details; they may be straight or curved and should be as short as possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lead lines must originate in immediate proximity to the reference character and extend to the feature indicated; must not cross each other. Lead lines are required for each reference character except those indicating the surface or cross section on which they are placed (such reference must be underlined to indicate absence of a lead line). Lead lines must be executed in the same way as drawing lines (see 1.84(l)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Arrows
rubrics_metrics.description: Arrows may be used at line ends provided their meaning is clear.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permitted uses: (1) freestanding arrow on a lead line to indicate the entire section it points to; (2) arrow touching a lead line to indicate the surface shown by the line looking along arrow direction; (3) to show direction of movement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Copyright or mask work notice
rubrics_metrics.description: A copyright or mask work notice may appear in the drawing within the sight immediately below the figure representing the protected material and limited to specific print sizes and content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Print size must be 0.32–0.64 cm high. Content limited to elements provided by law (e.g., '©1983 John Doe' or '*M* John Doe'). Inclusion permitted only if the authorization language required by §1.71(e) is included at the beginning of the specification. See §1.71(d)–(e) for the required authorization statement text.

rubrics_metrics.name: Numbering of sheets
rubrics_metrics.description: Sheets of drawings should be numbered in consecutive Arabic numerals starting with 1 within the sight; numbers must be placed in the middle of the top of the sheet but not in the margin (or right-hand side if view extends too close to middle).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sheet numbering must be clear and larger than reference character numbers. Use 'sheet_number/total_sheets' format, e.g., '2/6'. If sheet orientation is rotated per 1.84(i), sheet numbering must remain located per 1.84(t). PCT Rule 11.7 allows numbering at top or bottom and a different universal numbering approach; national-stage U.S. Office will accept international numbering conventions even if not U.S.-style.

rubrics_metrics.name: Numbering of views (figures)
rubrics_metrics.description: Different views must be numbered in consecutive Arabic numerals starting with 1, independent of sheet numbering, and preferably in the order they appear; partial views forming one complete view must be identified by the same number followed by a capital letter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: View numbers must be preceded by 'FIG.' Where only a single view is used it must not be numbered and 'FIG.' must not appear. Figure numbers/letters must be simple and clear, not associated with brackets/circles/quotes, and must be larger than reference character numbers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Security markings
rubrics_metrics.description: Authorized security markings may be placed on drawings provided they are outside the sight, preferably centered in the top margin.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Security markings are primarily Office responsibility; applicants may identify drawings with designations like NATO, TS, S, or C where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corrections on drawings (durability)
rubrics_metrics.description: Any corrections on drawings submitted must be durable and permanent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Special products for corrections may be used provided they are indelible and comply with other requirements (see 1.84(w) comments).

rubrics_metrics.name: No holes in drawing sheets
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants should not make holes in drawing sheets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not punch holes in sheets submitted to the Office.

rubrics_metrics.name: Types of drawings cross-reference
rubrics_metrics.description: Types of drawings (design drawings, plant drawings, reissue drawings) are governed by separate sections (§1.152, §1.165, §1.174).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult the cited sections for additional specific requirements relevant to design, plant, and reissue drawings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corrections to drawings: submission and timing (37 CFR 1.85)
rubrics_metrics.description: A utility or plant application will not be placed on the files for examination until objections to the drawings have been corrected; objections will not be held in abeyance and drawings filed after the application is placed on the files generally will not be included in the patent application publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If corrections are necessary, new corrected drawings must be submitted within the time set by the Office; the Office will not release drawings for correction. If a drawing does not comply at the time of allowance, the Office may set a three-month non-extendable period from the mail date of the notice of allowability within which applicant must file corrected/formal drawings to avoid abandonment. Applicants must reply to drawing requirements to avoid abandonment; voluntary drawings submitted after allowance and issue fee payment may or may not be printed depending on processing expediency and may require corresponding amendments to descriptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examination readiness requirement for drawings
rubrics_metrics.description: Drawings must be 'publication ready' with respect to pre-grant (eighteen-month) publication; objections to drawings will not be held in abeyance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must ensure drawings meet 1.84 requirements prior to filing or respond promptly to Office drawing requirements; failure to correct drawings when required may result in abandonment or delay in examination/publication.
